February 22, 1937. Morning Translation

China Evening News of February 21 (editorial) :-

"Atrocious Behaviour Of Italians"

The "more exciting" parts of the film
"Abyssinia" were deleted at the second review of the picture.
This shows that China did her best to please the aggressive
nation. During the screening of this film at the Isis
Theatre yesterday, about 100 Italian bluejackets and
civilians wrecked the cinema and injured some of the
employees and members of the audience.
In our view, this is a demonstration staged
by an aggressive nation in Chinese territory and constitutes
an insult to the Chinese government and people. It is
intolerable. The Chinese people have the right to exhibit
their sympathy towards Abyssinia; they also have their
reasons to abhor the acts of aggression committed against
that country. In all this, the Italian navy or people
have no right to interfere.
We hope that our government will immediately
lodge a strong protest and demand an apology, the punishment
of the persons responsible, and an assurance that acts of
this nature will not recur. We also hope that another
screening of the film "Abyssinia" will take place at an
early date and that more effective measures will be adopted
this time to deal with the rowdies of an aggressive nation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

DEATH ANNIVERSARY OF LIEUT. SHORT.

To-day being the 5th anniversary of the
death of Lieut. K.R. MacCawley Short, an American aviator,
who was killed in an aerial combat with Japanese aeroplanes
during the Shanghai War of January, 1932, local public
bodies will hold a memorial meeting to-day and will also
detail representatives to visit his tomb at the Hungjao
Aerodrome.

1937年2月22日。晨间译件

2月21日《字林西报》（社论）：-

“意大利人的暴行”

电影《阿比西尼亚》在第二次审查时，其“较为刺激”的部分被删减。这表明中国已尽力取悦该侵略国。昨日该片在伊西斯大戏院（Isis Theatre）放映期间，约100名意大利水兵和平民捣毁了电影院，并打伤了一些职员和观众。
在我方看来，这是侵略国在中国领土上策划的一次示威活动，构成了对中国政府和人民的侮辱。这是不可容忍的。中国人民有权表达对阿比西尼亚的同情；他们也有理由憎恶对该国实施的侵略行径。在所有这些事件中，意大利海军或民众均无权干涉。
我们希望我国政府立即提出强烈抗议，要求道歉、惩办责任人，并保证此类事件不再发生。我们也希望能尽早再次放映电影《阿比西尼亚》，且此次能采取更有效的措施来对付该侵略国的暴徒。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

肖特中尉逝世周年纪念。

今天是美国飞行员 K.R. MacCawley Short（音译：麦克考利·肖特）中尉逝世五周年纪念日，他于1932年1月上海战争期间在与日本飞机的空战中阵亡。本地公共团体将于今天举行追悼会，并将派代表前往虹桥机场他的墓地祭扫。

Shun Pao and other local newspapers dated Feb.20:

THE DEATH OF LIEUTENANT SHORT DURING THE SHANGHAI WAR

During the January 28 Incident, Lieutenant
Z.R. MacCawley Short, an American aviator, lost his life
in a fight with six enemy aeroplanes at Soochow.
Local Chinese officials and people together
with Mr. F.V. Wagnar, an intimate friend of the deceased,
are arranging the holding of a memorial service to Lieutenant
Short on Monday next (February 22) at the officer's tomb
near the Hungjao Aerodrome. Our country men will also
take part in the service to this foreign hero.

The Shanghai Evening News, dated April 10:-

Memorial Service for the deceased Mr. Short.

Local public bodies are preparing to hold a memorial
service tomorrow afternoon for Mr. Short, the deceased American aviator.
Mayor Wu Teh Chen and Chinese aviators will be requested to take part
in the service.

The public bodies will also erect a memorial to Mr.

purpose.

The mother and wife of Mr. Short will arrive at
Shanghai from America on April 19 and these public bodies are preparing
to welcome them on their arrival.

was killed in an air duel during the recent Sino-Japanese

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, MAY 13, 1932

Mrs. Short To
Leave For U.S.
This Morning

Chinese Government And
Citizens To Bid
Bon Voyage

Mrs. Elizabeth Short, mother of
the American aviator who lost his
life in an airplane battle with
Japanese airmen over Soochow, will
leave for the United States this
morning on the s.s. President
McKinley, accompanied by her son
Edmond. She will leave from the
Customs Jetty at 10.30 o'clock.

Representatives of the govern-
ment and various Chinese public
bodies will be present at the jetty
to give Mrs. Short a hearty send-
off and bon voyage.

Mrs. Short had tentatively decid-
ed to go to Peiping on a sightseeing
trip but changed her plans and
notified the members of the Robert
Short Memorial Committee that
she would go home directly. The
committee notified all bodies con-
cerned yesterday of the time of
her departure and asked them to
prepare flowers.

Mrs. Short came here on April
18 and amid a big crowd of wel-
comers was ushered into the
Cathay Hotel where she has been
staying ever since, being the
"nation's guest" for the first time
in Chinese history as a foreign
woman. She has been greatly ad-
mired and deeply sympathized by
both the Chinese government and
its people.

While here she participated in
the funeral ceremonies of her son
who now lies buried on Chinese
soil. She also received her a
testimonial in memory of her
husband and their family estab-
lished at Soochow and a "living
memorial" — the Robert Short
Memorial Educational Foundation.

肖特夫人
今晨启程
赴美

中国政府及
市民将
为之送行

伊丽莎白·肖特夫人，那位在苏州上空与日本飞行员空战中丧生的美国飞行员的母亲，将于今晨由其子埃德蒙（Edmond）陪同，乘坐“麦金莱总统”号轮船前往美国。她将于10点30分从海关码头出发。

政府代表及各中国公共团体代表将出席码头，热烈欢送肖特夫人并祝其一路顺风。

肖特夫人曾暂定前往北平观光，但改变了计划，并通知罗伯特·肖特纪念委员会成员她将直接回国。委员会昨日已通知所有相关机构其出发时间，并请他们准备鲜花。

肖特夫人于4月18日抵达此地，在众多欢迎者的簇拥下入住华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel），此后一直居住于此，成为中国历史上首位作为“国家贵宾”的外国女性。她深受中国政府及人民的钦佩和深切同情。

在此期间，她参加了其子的葬礼，其子现安葬于中国土地之下。她还收到了一份纪念其丈夫及其在苏州建立的家庭的证书，以及一份“活纪念碑”——罗伯特·肖特纪念教育基金会。

Made by P.S.Pitts. Forwarded by [Signature]

The following tentative arrangements have been made by
the "Robert Short Memorial Committee" for the funeral of the
late Lieut. Robert Short, American aviator killed during the
recent Sino-Japanese conflict:-
The funeral service will be held at 2 p.m. Sunday April
24, 1932, at the Moore Memorial Church on Thibet Road. Burial
will be at the Hungjao Aerodrome.
Arrangements have been made to accomodate 1000 persons at
the funeral service.
At approximately 3 p.m. the funeral procession will pro-
ceed on foot from the Moore Memorial Church along Thibet Road into
Bubbling Well Road and will continue to Ferry Road where a halt
will be called to enable the majority of the mourners to continue
to Hungjao in motor-cars. From Ferry Road to the Aerodrome the
procession will move via Bubbling Well, Great Western, Chungshen
and Hungjao Roads.
I am informed that application has been made by Mr. O.K.Yui
of the "Robert Short Memorial Committee", to the Shanghai Municipal
Council for the necessary Police assistance and co-operation, and
that the order of the procession will be as follows:-
Shanghai Municipal Police Mounted Escort.
Chinese detachment of the Shanghai Municipal Police(if possible)
Shanghai Volunteer Corps - American and Chinese Companies.
Band of the Bureau of Public Safety of Greater Shanghai.
Pall Bearers consisting of 4 Chinese and 4 American aviators.
Honorary Pall Bearers.
Chief Mourners and Officials.
Representatives of the People's Organisations and friends.
Vehicles containing floral tributes.

Subject (in full) Arrival of Mrs. Short.

Made by P.S. Pitts. Forwarded by D. O. Tarrant

Mrs. Elizabeth Short, mother of Robert Short, American
aviator who was killed during the recent Sino-Japanese hos-
tilities, arrived in Shanghai at 1.30 p.m. April 19, 1932
by the s.s. "President Loft" which berthed at the Dollar
Wharf, Pootung.

A deputation representing the National Government and
86 Public Organisations, and headed by Mr. H.O.Tong, Chair-
man of the "Robert Short Memorial Committee", welcomed Mrs.
Short to China immediately upon her arrival.

Mrs. Short was accompanied by members of the "Committee
of Welcome" on the Whangpoo Conservancy Board's tender "Li
Pei" to the Customs Jetty, where she was met by the Committees
of various local Chinese Organisations. After inspecting a
guard-of-honour of Chinese Boy Scouts and Girl Guides Mrs.
Short expressed her appreciation of the kindnesses shown her
by the Chinese people. She was then driven away to the
Cathay Hotel without further incident.

I attach herewith a list showing the names of the
members of the "Committee of Welcome" and the bodies which
they represent, and a copy of the speech made by Mr. H.O.Tong
upon Mrs. Short's arrival.

P.S. Pitts.

Speech by Mr. H. O. Tong,
Chairman of Robert Short Memorial Committee.

Mrs. Short,

On behalf of the Government and people of
China, which are represented in this group, I have
the honour of extending to you a cordial welcome to our
country, and to express to you the very deep sense of
appreciation which is felt by our nation of the sacrifice
which unites our sentiments with yours.

We have come to receive you in the name of
our people, and to escort you ashore where a represent-
ative gathering waits to welcome you.

The depth of our nation's gratitude will be
shown to you during your sojourn amongst us. It is our
honour now to be granted the privilege of greeting you
upon your arrival to our shores, and to introduce you
to a grateful people.

肖特夫人，

我代表在此群体中体现的中国政府和人民，荣幸地向您表示热烈欢迎您来到我国，并向您表达我国对您那份将我们的情感与您紧密相连的牺牲所怀有的深切感激之情。

我们代表我国人民前来迎接您，并护送您上岸，那里有一个具有代表性的集会正等待着欢迎您。

在您逗留期间，您将看到我国感激之情的深度。此刻，我们荣幸地获得在您抵达我国海岸时向您致意并将您介绍给充满感激之情的人民的特权。

Subject (in full) Arrival of Mrs. Short.

Made by F.S.Pitts. Forwarded by （签名）

In connection with the arrival of Mrs. Short, mother
of Robert Short, who was killed whilst flying in a Chinese
aeroplane during the recent Sino-Japanese hostilities, I
have to report the following:-

Mrs. Short, who is accompanied by her young son, is
due to arrive in Shanghai on April 19, 1932, by the s.s.
"President Taft", which will berth at the Dollar Wharf at
approximately noon on that date.

At 11 a.m., a Customs launch will leave the Customs
Jetty containing some fifteen members of the National
Government and Public Organisations with the object of
welcoming Mrs. Short to Shanghai. This committee of wel-
come will be headed by Mr. H.O.Tong, Chairman of the
"Robert Short Memorial Committee", and will meet the "Pres-
ident Taft" before she berths. The Customs launch is ex-
pected to arrive back at the Customs Jetty at noon with Mrs.
Short on board.

Some 200 members of various local organisations are
expected to congregate within the precincts of the Jetty
in order to welcome Mrs. Short, whilst a still larger number
will be waiting outside the entrance to the Jetty.

After her arrival Mrs. Short will stay at the Cathay
Hotel, Rooms Nos. 633 and 640, where she will be attended
by three representatives of the Nationalist Government -
one lady and two gentlemen.

No public functions will be held in her honour until after
her son's funeral, which has tentatively been fixed for the
April 24, 1932.

I attach herewith a newspaper cutting dated April 16, 1932.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, APRIL 16, 1932

MRS. E. SHORT
DUE TUESDAY

National Delegation to
Welcome Guest

Preparations to welcome Mrs.
Elizabeth Short and arrangements
for her visit while in China have
been practically completed by the
general committee appointed by the
Government recently to look after
her arrival and sojourn here.

Mrs. Short, mother of the Ameri-
can aviator Lieut. Robert Short, is
travelling on the Dollar liner,
President Taft, expected here next
Tuesday. Upon her arrival, she
will be an official guest of the na-
tion. Lieut. Short, it may be re-
membered, died in an aerial com-
bat with a Japanese air squadron
over Soochow during the recent
Sino-Japanese hostilities.

Mrs. Short comes out to China to
attend the funeral of her son. Tri-
butes of gratitude from the Gov-
ernment and people of China are
to be extended to her. General Wu
Te-chen, Mayor of Greater Shang-
hai and representatives of local
public organisations will meet Mrs.
Short at the Customs jetty.

The personnel of the general com-
mittee includes: Messrs. H. O.

由政府最近任命的一般委员会负责照顾肖特夫人抵达及在华逗留事宜，该委员会已基本完成欢迎伊丽莎白·肖特夫人及安排其在华访问的准备工作。

肖特夫人是美国飞行员罗伯特·肖特中尉的母亲，她乘坐美元轮船公司（Dollar Line）的“塔夫脱总统号”轮船旅行，预计下周二抵达。抵达后，她将成为国家的官方贵宾。人们可能还记得，肖特中尉在近期的中日敌对行动期间，于苏州上空与日本空军中队进行空战时牺牲。

肖特夫人来华参加其儿子的葬礼。中国政府和人民将向她致以感激的敬意。大上海市长吴铁城将军及当地公共团体的代表将在海关码头迎接肖特夫人。

一般委员会的成员包括：代表国民政府的童杭时先生（H. O. Teng）；代表军队的王赓将军（Gaston Wang）；代表航空队的沈德燮上校（T. H. Shen）；代表财政部的张履鳌（Loy Chang）；代表外交部的郭泰祺（T. W. Kwok）；代表大上海市政府的俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui）；以及代表本市各民众团体的袁履登（T. L. Yuan）、吴荣第（R. Y. Wu）、吴蕴斋（Y. C. Woo）、莫永乾（E. K. Moy）、梁寒操（Hubert S. Liang）、应昌世（C. L. Ying）、刘湛恩（Herman Liu）、黄惠平（T. P. Wong）和黄申锡（S. S. Huang）。

据悉，将在海关码头迎接肖特夫人的各组织代表，仅凭由罗伯特·肖特纪念委员会在其新闸路135号总部签发的通行证方可进入码头围场。
